page.layout: One printed page, numbered 271 at top right. One text block of full-width running paragraphs. Each paragraph opens with a roman lead phrase, then "]" and an italic summary. Centred chapter headings CAP. XVII., CAP. XVIII., CAP. XX., CAP. XXI., each followed by its title and summary. No margin notes, no running head, no catchword, no signature.

Pars.maxima subsignarent.] Cum alia Lege in Anglia initiari Sacris Ordinibus non possint.
Quod pro Me totics Orare instituit.] Ter enim vel quater in Matutino Officio pro Rege oratur.
main_text.head: CAP. XVII. Christi Gubernationis ; Sceptri. ] Quibus Libri eorum & Concionces abundant.

CAP. XVIII. Tractatu Uxbrigensi.] Uxbrigia Oppidum in Anglia inter Oxonium (in qua Rextum agebat) & Londinum media, in qua tertio jam Belli Anno missis utrinque Delegatis agebatur de Pace, sed cum nihil aequi impetrari potuisset, frustra.

CAP. XX. Conventus Theologorum Insolito more.] Quia mos solitus & legitimus erat, ut Mandato Regis praecunte[?], certi Theologi a Clero in suis seor-sim Provinciis deputarentur in Synodum, quae sua Jura & Privilegia habebat, cum jam pauci essent duntaxat in Concilium vocati quos Uter-que Confessius nominaverat.
CAP. XXI. Literas meas interceptas.]

page.notes: Italic extent in the summaries and in the body of the first paragraph is approximate; the italic/roman boundary inside "caeterarumque Sacrarum Celebrationum, permissa Verborum Libertate." is uncertain. Long s has been written as plain s throughout (e.g. "possint", "Christi", "Tractatu", "potuisset"), although the printer used long s with ff ligature forms. "praecunte" and "Rextum" are uncertain readings. The page ends with "infe-" mid-word, which continues on the next page. The headings are one <head> per chapter, each number and title together.
